Rheumatology · published research

Achilles tendinitis

Clinical results are mixed. A 2025 randomized trial found no added three-month symptom benefit from PBM combined with exercise and radial pressure waves versus exercise alone. Earlier trials report both positive and null outcomes, and pooled Achilles evidence remains uncertain.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Clinical results are mixed. A 2025 randomized trial found no added three-month symptom benefit from PBM combined with exercise and radial pressure waves versus exercise alone. Earlier trials report both positive and null outcomes, and pooled Achilles evidence remains uncertain.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Tendons > Achilles tendon category contains 81 source-database titles. A web check adds the 2025 results paper linked to an existing trial protocol, for 82 unique publications. The set includes 13 human outcome reports, 61 animal studies, six reviews or meta-analyses, one protocol, and one editorial or other study-design item. One animal publication also contains a cell arm, so method counts overlap.

Human and clinical evidence

Human reports cover chronic tendinopathy, tendon rupture rehabilitation, and immediate tendon physiology rather than one uniform indication. A meta-analysis of four trials and 119 participants found low-to-very-low certainty and no convincing durable advantage on key function outcomes (Martimbianco et al. 2020). In a 2025 randomized trial of 46 runners, adding PBM to exercise and radial pressure-wave therapy did not improve three-month VISA-A symptoms more than exercise alone; exercise plus pressure waves showed the larger improvement (Tenforde et al. 2025). A 60-person 2024 trial and earlier exercise-combination trials add mixed findings (Shriya et al. 2024 Tumilty et al. 2016). The protocol and results paper share trial registration and are one cohort, not two trials.

Animal evidence

Most animal work uses rat tendon injury, tendinitis, or repair models, with smaller rabbit and mouse sets. Many report changes in collagen organization, inflammatory markers, or mechanical repair, while some report limited or null functional effects. These experiments do not override mixed human results.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One porcine tendon-fibroblast experiment reports cellular responses to light. A separate animal publication also contains cell methods. Neither is evidence of clinical tendon recovery.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Protocols vary across red and near-infrared lasers or LEDs, single treatments and repeated courses, local or broader application, and exercise or other co-interventions. Wavelength is the light's color band and affects tissue penetration. The parameters and tendon conditions are too varied to infer one effective clinical dose.

Interpretation

The large animal literature supports biological investigation, while direct human evidence remains limited and inconsistent. Current evidence does not establish routine PBM benefit for Achilles tendinopathy or tendon rupture. Trials should isolate PBM from co-interventions and follow pain, function, return to activity, and recurrence.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for added short-term symptom or function improvement in Achilles tendinopathy because randomized trials and pooled estimates are mixed Very low for durable benefit, isolated PBM, or tendon-rupture recovery
Publications and records82 publications (81 exact database titles plus 1 linked 2025 results paper)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The evidence includes many animal papers but few comparable human trials. A pooled review found low-to-very-low certainty, and a 2025 trial found no added benefit from PBM when combined with exercise and pressure waves. More independent sham-controlled trials should isolate PBM and measure recovery over months.
